title: from_credentials guard weaker than precondition doc
description: from_credentials checks parse_bcrypt_cost (no length check) but doc Preconditions say callers should pre-validate with looks_like_bcrypt_hash (which also checks len >= 60). A hash shorter than 60 chars with a valid cost field — e.g. '$2b$10$tooshort' — will not panic, will be stored, and bcrypt::verify will silently return false for all auth attempts for that user. Config::validate() catches this via looks_like_bcrypt_hash before the production code path reaches from_credentials, so no known exploit exists through the normal startup path. But from_credentials is also called from imap/session/auth.rs (test path), integration tests, and could be called from a future code path that bypasses validation. Fix: change the internal guard in from_credentials from parse_bcrypt_cost to looks_like_bcrypt_hash, matching the stated precondition and the check in from_content.
